abstract.p: A two-part affine approximation has been found to be a good approximation for transformer computations over certain subjectobject relations. Adapting the Bigger Analogy Test Set, we show that the linear transformation W s, where s is a middle layer representation of a subject token and W is derived from model derivatives, is also able to accurately reproduce final object states for many relations. This linear technique is able to achieve 90% faithfulness on morphological relations, and we show similar findings multilingually and across models. Our findings indicate that some conceptual relationships in language models, such as morphology, are readily interpretable from latent space, and are sparsely encoded by cross-layer linear transformations.
